unit: EUR bn per year, 2026 = January-August; low/central/high
replaces: refugees_net.json countries.{DNK,SWE,ITA}.gross (and round4b.json refugees.{DNK,SWE,ITA}, which it copies); same {year: {low, central, high}} shape. DNK also gets new revenue_model_inputs.employment_rate.

DNK.basis: official components: OECD DAC in-donor refugee costs (rise over 2021, first-year ODA-eligible costs) + the municipal block-grant compensation agreed by the government and KL; central counts 70% of the municipal frame to allow overlap; high x1.3 for benefits beyond 12 months and regional health care

municipal_frame_dkk_bn.2022: 1.4 (Ukraine and COVID together; Ukraine part taken as ~1.0)

revenue_model_inputs_employment_rate.basis: Statistics Denmark: about one third of 18-64-year-olds in wage employment in Q3 2022, 58% in Q3 2024 (12,100 people); annual averages interpolated, later years +2-3 points

SWE.basis: Migration Agency annual reports: total cost of reception and support of people with temporary protection (2022 ~SEK 2.0bn plus the SEK 0.5bn one-off municipal grant; 2023 1,875m; 2024 1,534m; 2025 486m) plus, for 2025, the municipal resettlement lump sums paid for Ukrainians once registered (est. SEK 0.8bn, 0.3-1.0); central x1.25 for regional health care and other costs outside the Agency line; high = max(x1.7, the rise in Sweden's DAC in-donor refugee costs over 2021, OECD's 2022 estimate EUR 0.325bn)

ITA.basis: national appropriations in the Ukraine decree-laws (DL 21/2022, DL 50/2022, DL 16/2023) as summarised by the Chamber of Deputies research service; these are spending caps, so the low end allows for under-spending (unused accoglienza diffusa places were reallocated in 2023). EU pre-financing stays in round4b eu_funded
